name: How are electrical outlets handled during a backsplash installation?

mainEntity.name: How are electrical outlets handled during a backsplash installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need box extenders because adding tile and mortar pushes the wall surface forward by a quarter to a half inch. Building codes require electrical junction boxes to sit flush with or within a quarter inch of the finished wall surface to prevent fire hazards and ensure stability. Standard practice involves switching off the circuit breaker, adding non-conductive plastic or metal box extenders, and resecuring the outlets so faceplates mount flat against the new tile.
acceptedAnswer.description: Electrical box extenders are installed so outlets and switches sit flush with the new tile surface, complying with safety codes.
